source_text: Omnia autem ista credo ignota eis, qui ad nostra turbantur, aut sola forsitan lectione, non etiam intentione comperta secundum maiorem uim imperitorum apud gloriosissimam scilicet multitudinem psychicorum. propterea per singulas direximus species ieiunationum, xerophagiarum, stationum, ut, dum recensemus secundum utriusque testamenti paraturam, . quantum proficiant recusati uel recisi uel retardati pabuli officia, eos retundamus, qui haec uelut uacantia infirmant, item dum pariter ostendimus, quo semper in ordine fuerint religionis, eos reuincamus, qui haec ut noua accusant; nec nouum enim quod semper nec uacuum quod utile. sed et illud in medio est, quaedam ex his officiis a deo homini imperata legem constituisse, quaedam ab homine deo oblata uotum expunxisse. tamen et uotum, cum a deo acceptatum est, legem in posterum facit. per auctoritatem acceptatoris; exinde enim faciendum mandauit qui factum comprobauit. itaque et hinc in alia specie altercatio diuersae partis obducitur, cum dicunt: aut pseudoprophetia est, si spiritalis uox sollemnia ista constituit, aut haeresis, si humana ! praesumptio adinuenit. eam enim formam reprehendentes, qua et uetera decucurrerunt, et ex ea retorquentes, quae et aduersarii ueterum aduersus illa poterunt retractare, aut et illa recusare debebunt aut exerta ista suscipere; necessarie maxime cum et ista, a quocumque institutore sunt siue spiritali siue tantum fideli, eidem deo currant, cui et uetera. indubitate enim et haeresis et pseudoprophetia diuinitatis diuersitate iudicabuntur apud nos omnes unici dei creatoris et Christi eius antistites, adeoque indifferenter hanc partem defendo illis offerens in quo uelint gradum figere. spiritus diaboli est, dicis, o psychice. et quomodo dei nostri officia indicit nec alii offerenda quam deo nostro? aut contende diabolum cum deo facere nostro aut satanas paracletus habeatur. sed hominem antichristum adfirmas; hoc enim uocantur haeretici nomine penes Iohannem. et quomodo, quisquis ille est, in Christo nostro haec erga dominum nostrum officia disposuit, cum et antichristi erga deum, aduersum nostrum processerint Christum? quo itaque putas laterum confirmatum apud nos spiritum, cum imperat an cum probat, quae deus noster et imperauit semper et probauit? sed rursus palos terminales figitis deo, sicut de gratia, ita de disciplina, sicut de charismatibus, ita et de sollemnibus, ut perinde officia cessauerint, quemadmodum et beneficia eius, atque ita negetis usque adhuc eum munia imponere, quia et hic lex et prophetae usque ad Iohannem. superest ut totum auferatis, quantum in uobis, tam otiosum.
thought_title: The opponents' objection and the defense of the observances' authority
orientation: Tertullian is answering the unspiritual Christians who object that the fasts, dry-food fasts, and station fasts are either false prophecy or heresy, and he is showing that these practices belong to the same God as the old observances.
pass_a_gloss: But all these things, I believe, are unknown to them, who are disturbed at our practices, or perhaps have been learned by reading alone, not also by attention, according to the greater force of the inexperienced among the most glorious, of course, multitude of the unspiritual Christians. Therefore we have directed our discussion through the individual kinds of fastings, of dry-food fasts, of station fasts, so that, while we review according to the preparation of each testament, how much the duties of refused or cut back or delayed food profit, we may blunt those who weaken these things as empty, likewise while we show at the same time in what order they have always been in religion, we may refute those who accuse these things as new; for neither is what is always new, nor is what is useful empty. But also this is in the middle, that some of these duties commanded by God to man have established a law, some offered by man to God have discharged a vow. Nevertheless also a vow, when it has been accepted by God, makes a law for the future through the authority of the acceptor; for from then on he commanded that it be done who approved that it was done. And so also from this point in another kind the dispute of the opposing party is brought forward, when they say: either it is false prophecy, if a spiritual voice has established these solemn observances, or it is heresy, if human presumption has invented them. For while they reprove that form by which also the old things ran their course, and while they twist back from it those things which also the adversaries of the old things will be able to retract against those things, either they ought to refuse also those old things or to receive these things openly; necessarily especially since also these things, from whatever institutor they are, whether spiritual or only faithful, run to the same God, to whom also the old things run. For without doubt both heresy and false prophecy will be judged by a difference of divinity among us all, priests of the one God the creator and of his Christ, and so far indifferently I defend this side, offering to them in what they wish to fix their step. It is the spirit of the devil, you say, O unspiritual Christian. And how does he prescribe the duties of our God, and duties not to be offered to another than to our God? Either contend that the devil acts with our God, or let Satan be considered the Advocate. But you assert that he is a man, an antichrist; for by this name heretics are called in John. And how, whoever he is, has he arranged in our Christ these duties toward our Lord, since also antichrists have proceeded against our Christ, against God? In what way therefore do you think the spirit is confirmed among us by the flanks, when he commands or when he approves those things which our God has both always commanded and approved? But again you fix boundary posts for God, as concerning grace, so concerning discipline, as concerning gifts, so also concerning solemn observances, so that in like manner the duties have ceased, just as also his benefits have ceased, and so you deny that up to now he imposes services, because also here the law and the prophets were until John. It remains that you take away the whole, as much as is in you, as idle.

pass_b_english: But I believe all these things are unknown to those who are disturbed by our practices. Or perhaps they have learned them only by reading, not by understanding, according to the greater influence of the inexperienced among that most glorious crowd, the unspiritual Christians. For this reason I have gone through each kind of observance: fasts, dry-food fasts, and station fasts. My purpose is this: while I review how much the duties of food, refused, cut back, or delayed, accomplish according to the arrangement of both testaments, I may blunt those who weaken these practices as if they were empty. At the same time, by showing that they have always held a place in true religion, I may refute those who accuse them of being new. For what has always existed is not new, and what is useful is not empty.

But there is also this point in the middle: some of these observances were commanded by God to humanity and so became law, while others were offered by humanity to God and so discharged a vow. Yet even a vow, when it has been accepted by God, becomes law for the future through the authority of the one who accepted it. For from that point on, the one who approved the deed commanded that it be done.

And so here another objection from the opposing side is brought forward in a different form. They say: either it is false prophecy, if a spiritual voice established these solemn observances, or it is heresy, if human presumption invented them. For they criticize the very pattern by which the old practices also came down to us, and by twisting this argument they could use it against the old practices as well, the same arguments that adversaries of the old ways could raise against them. So either they must reject those old practices too, or they must openly accept these new ones. This is especially necessary since these practices, from whatever founder they come, whether spiritual or merely faithful, run toward the same God as the old ones did. For without doubt both heresy and false prophecy will be judged by us, all of us priests of the one God the Creator and of his Christ, by their divergence from the divine nature. And so I defend this side without distinction, offering them whatever ground they wish to plant their foot on.

You say, O unspiritual Christian, that it is the spirit of the devil. And how does it prescribe duties belonging to our God, duties not to be offered to anyone but our God? Either argue that the devil works with our God, or let Satan be considered the Advocate. But you assert that he is a human antichrist, for this is the name heretics are called by in John. And how is it that whoever he is, he arranged these duties toward our Lord in our Christ, when antichrists have proceeded toward God but against our Christ? By what flanks, then, do you think the Spirit is confirmed among us, when he commands, or when he approves, the things that our God has both always commanded and always approved?

But again you fix boundary posts for God: for grace, so also for discipline; for spiritual gifts, so also for solemn observances, so that his duties have ceased just as his benefits have, and so you deny that he still imposes obligations, because here too the law and the prophets were until John. It remains for you to take away everything, as far as it lies in you, so idle.

problems.quote: as is the greater failing of the inexperienced
problems.why: 'uis' here means 'force/influence/number', not 'failing'; the inexperienced have greater sway among the crowd.
problems.fix: according to the greater influence of the inexperienced
problems.ruling: Latin "maiorem vim imperitorum" = greater force/influence of the inexperienced, not "greater failing".

problems.quote: And how is it that whoever he is, he arranged these duties toward our Lord in our Christ, when antichrists have proceeded against our Christ in their dealings with God?
problems.source_quote: et quomodo, quisquis ille est, in Christo nostro haec erga dominum nostrum officia disposuit, cum et antichristi erga deum, aduersum nostrum processerint Christum?
problems.why: 'in Christo nostro' goes with 'disposuit' (arranged in our Christ), not 'our Lord'; 'erga deum' and 'aduersum nostrum Christum' are paired: antichrists proceed toward God but against our Christ.
problems.fix: how has whoever he is arranged these duties toward our Lord in our Christ, when antichrists have proceeded toward God but against our Christ?
problems.ruling: Latin pairs "erga deum" with antichrists and "adversum nostrum Christum"; English conflates them, altering contrast.

problems.why: 'Tam otiosum' agrees with 'totum' (everything): 'so idle'—you make everything idle, not God specifically.
problems.ruling: "tam otiosum" modifies "totum", not God; translation misidentifies referent.

problems.ruling: Latin 'quia et hic lex et prophetae usque ad Iohannem' lacks any scripture reference; English adds '(Matthew 11:13)' absent from source.

last_rejected.quote: By what flanks, then, do you think the Spirit is confirmed among us
last_rejected.source_quote: quo itaque putas laterum confirmatum apud nos spiritum
last_rejected.why: 'laterum' likely means 'on either side/flank' i.e., from whichever angle; 'flanks' as literal body-sides is obscure here.
last_rejected.fix: From what side, then, do you think the Spirit is confirmed among us
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'laterum' = 'of sides/flanks'; translation captures sense though 'flanks' is literal, meaning unchanged

last_rejected.quote: according to the greater influence of the inexperienced among that most glorious crowd, the unspiritual Christians
last_rejected.source_quote: secundum maiorem uim imperitorum apud gloriosissimam scilicet multitudinem psychicorum
last_rejected.why: Latin says “the greater power of the leaders/authorities,” not “inexperienced”; adds a qualifier not in source.
last_rejected.fix: according to the greater power of the leaders among that most glorious crowd of unspiritual Christians
last_rejected.ruling: imperitorum = 'inexperienced/ignorant'; no added qualifier. 'influence' for uim is within normal range.
